defaults.permitted_development: Detached outbuildings such as sheds, workshops and garden stores can usually be permitted development in England where they are for a purpose incidental to the enjoyment of the house, stay behind the principal elevation, remain single storey and comply with the Class E height and coverage limits. The route does not cover separate self-contained living accommodation.

rules.height_rules: Keep the building single storey with eaves no higher than 2.5m. The overall height limit is 4m for a dual-pitched roof, 3m for any other roof and 2.5m overall if any part sits within 2m of a boundary.
rules.depth_rules: There is no standalone depth allowance. The key tests are whether the building stays within the curtilage, remains behind the principal elevation and keeps the total area covered by additions and outbuildings within 50% of the land around the original house.
rules.boundary_rules: Boundary siting matters because any part within 2m of a boundary is capped at 2.5m overall. On designated land, outbuildings at the side of the house can need permission, and any outbuilding in the curtilage of a listed building needs planning permission.
rules.roof_rules: Roof form directly controls the allowed height. A dual-pitched roof can go to 4m, other roofs to 3m, but any part within 2m of a boundary must stay at or below 2.5m overall. Verandas, balconies and raised platforms above 300mm are outside the normal Class E route.
rules.materials_rules: Materials do not have to match exactly, but the building should still read as subordinate and domestic in character. The layout, services and fittings should stay incidental so the structure does not drift into self-contained accommodation.

rules.permitted_development: A detached outbuilding can usually stay within householder permitted development if it is for a purpose incidental to the house, sits behind the principal elevation and meets the Class E height and coverage limits. That route does not cover a separate dwelling or self-contained annexe.

rules.height_rules: Use the Class E height envelope: single storey only, eaves no higher than 2.5m, up to 4m overall with a dual-pitched roof or 3m with any other roof, dropping to 2.5m overall if any part is within 2m of a boundary.
rules.depth_rules: There is no standalone depth allowance for an outbuilding. The practical tests are whether it stays within the residential curtilage, remains behind the principal elevation and keeps total coverage by additions and outbuildings within 50% of the land around the original house.
rules.boundary_rules: Boundary siting is often the deciding issue. Within 2m of a boundary the overall height must stay at or below 2.5m; on designated land, side-garden outbuildings and structures more than 20m from the house face tighter limits.
rules.roof_rules: Keep the building single storey and the roof simple. A dual-pitched roof can go to 4m; other roof forms top out at 3m, and any veranda, balcony or raised platform would fall outside ordinary outbuilding permitted development.
rules.materials_rules: The building should read as subordinate to the house and remain incidental in use. Match or complement the host dwelling where visible, and avoid a layout or servicing package that makes it function as self-contained living accommodation.

rules.permitted_development: Householder permitted development can often cover a shed, garage, studio or similar detached building, but only while it remains incidental to the dwellinghouse and stays within the Class E siting, height and 50% coverage limits. It is not a route to separate living accommodation.

rules.height_rules: The usual height limits are single storey only, eaves up to 2.5m, 4m overall for a dual-pitched roof and 3m for other roof forms. If any part sits within 2m of a boundary, the overall height should stay at or below 2.5m.
rules.depth_rules: Outbuildings do not have a separate depth rule in the way extensions do. The real checks are curtilage location, remaining behind the principal elevation and staying within the overall 50% coverage limit for buildings and additions around the original house.
rules.boundary_rules: Most boundary problems come from height and prominence. Any part within 2m of the boundary is limited to 2.5m overall, and designated land has extra controls for side-garden positions and buildings set more than 20m from the house.
rules.roof_rules: Roof form affects the height limit directly: up to 4m overall for a dual-pitched roof, 3m for other roof types and only 2.5m overall where the building is within 2m of a boundary. Verandas, balconies and raised platforms are outside the normal outbuilding right.
rules.materials_rules: Use finishes that sit comfortably with the house and garden setting, especially on visible elevations. The design should still look like an incidental outbuilding rather than a standalone dwelling with its own living facilities.

rules.permitted_development: An outbuilding is often acceptable under the normal householder rules where it stays single storey, remains subordinate to the house and is used only for incidental domestic purposes. Once it starts functioning as self-contained living space, planning permission is usually needed.

rules.height_rules: For an outbuilding relying on ordinary householder rights, keep it single storey, with eaves no more than 2.5m high, a 4m cap for a dual-pitched roof and a 3m cap for other roofs. Boundary siting within 2m reduces the overall limit to 2.5m.
rules.depth_rules: Instead of a fixed depth limit, the key outbuilding tests are position within the curtilage, not building forward of the principal elevation and not pushing total site coverage by additions and outbuildings beyond 50% of the land around the original house.
rules.boundary_rules: If the building is tight to a boundary, design around the 2.5m overall height cap. Also remember that designated land brings extra restrictions for side locations and for some structures placed well away from the house.
rules.roof_rules: The safest route is a modest single-storey roof. Dual-pitched forms can reach 4m, other roofs 3m, but boundary siting can reduce that to 2.5m overall. Raised platforms, balconies and similar features are not part of the ordinary Class E outbuilding route.
rules.materials_rules: Materials do not have to copy the house exactly, but the building should still look subordinate and domestic in character. Keep the layout and services incidental so it does not drift into self-contained accommodation.

rules.height_rules: Use the Class E height envelope: single storey only, eaves no higher than 2.5m, up to 4m overall with a dual-pitched roof or 3m with any other roof, dropping to 2.5m overall if any part is within 2m of a boundary.
rules.depth_rules: There is no standalone depth allowance for an outbuilding. The practical tests are whether it stays within the residential curtilage, remains behind the principal elevation and keeps total coverage by additions and outbuildings within 50% of the land around the original house.
rules.boundary_rules: Boundary siting is often the deciding issue. Within 2m of a boundary the overall height must stay at or below 2.5m; on designated land, side-garden outbuildings and structures more than 20m from the house face tighter limits.
rules.roof_rules: Keep the building single storey and the roof simple. A dual-pitched roof can go to 4m; other roof forms top out at 3m, and any veranda, balcony or raised platform would fall outside ordinary outbuilding permitted development.
rules.materials_rules: The building should read as subordinate to the house and remain incidental in use. Match or complement the host dwelling where visible, and avoid a layout or servicing package that makes it function as self-contained living accommodation.

rules.permitted_development: An outbuilding is often acceptable under the normal householder rules where it stays single storey, remains subordinate to the house and is used only for incidental domestic purposes. Once it starts functioning as self-contained living space, planning permission is usually needed.

rules.height_rules: For an outbuilding relying on ordinary householder rights, keep it single storey, with eaves no more than 2.5m high, a 4m cap for a dual-pitched roof and a 3m cap for other roofs. Boundary siting within 2m reduces the overall limit to 2.5m.
rules.depth_rules: Instead of a fixed depth limit, the key outbuilding tests are position within the curtilage, not building forward of the principal elevation and not pushing total site coverage by additions and outbuildings beyond 50% of the land around the original house.
rules.boundary_rules: If the building is tight to a boundary, design around the 2.5m overall height cap. Also remember that designated land brings extra restrictions for side locations and for some structures placed well away from the house.
rules.roof_rules: The safest route is a modest single-storey roof. Dual-pitched forms can reach 4m, other roofs 3m, but boundary siting can reduce that to 2.5m overall. Raised platforms, balconies and similar features are not part of the ordinary Class E outbuilding route.
rules.materials_rules: Materials do not have to copy the house exactly, but the building should still look subordinate and domestic in character. Keep the layout and services incidental so it does not drift into self-contained accommodation.

rules.permitted_development: Householder permitted development can often cover a shed, garage, studio or similar detached building, but only while it remains incidental to the dwellinghouse and stays within the Class E siting, height and 50% coverage limits. rules.depth_rules: Outbuildings do not have a separate depth rule in the way extensions do. The real checks are curtilage location, remaining behind the principal elevation and staying within the overall 50% coverage limit for buildings and additions around the original house.
rules.boundary_rules: Most boundary problems come from height and prominence. Any part within 2m of the boundary is limited to 2.5m overall, and designated land has extra controls for side-garden positions and buildings set more than 20m from the house.
rules.roof_rules: Roof form affects the height limit directly: up to 4m overall for a dual-pitched roof, 3m for other roof types and only 2.5m overall where the building is within 2m of a boundary. Verandas, balconies and raised platforms are outside the normal outbuilding right.
rules.materials_rules: Use finishes that sit comfortably with the house and garden setting, especially on visible elevations. The design should still look like an incidental outbuilding rather than a standalone dwelling with its own living facilities.
